description: SOC-thermal voltage model: V = OCV(SOC) - I*R(T), with Arrhenius resistance and capacity correction

cell.name: Generic Li-S pouch cell
cell.source: Wild et al. (2015), Energy Environ. Sci. 8, 3477; Mikhaylik & Akridge (2004), J. Electrochem. Soc. 151, A1969

capacity_ref.note: Nominal capacity at T_ref (theoretical 1675 mAh/g, practical ~600 mAh/g)

R_ref.note: Internal resistance at T_ref (298.15 K); higher than Li-ion due to poor sulfur conductivity

ocv_coefficients.description: OCV(SOC) = a0 + a1*SOC + a2*SOC^2 + a3*SOC^3 + a4*SOC^4 + a5*SOC^5
ocv_coefficients.source: Fitted to Li-S two-plateau OCV profile; upper plateau ~2.4V (S8 to Li2S4), lower plateau ~2.1V (Li2S4 to Li2S)

E_a.note: Activation energy; higher than Li-ion because polysulfide dissolution kinetics are thermally activated
E_a.source: Mikhaylik & Akridge (2004), J. Electrochem. Soc. 151, A1969; Kumaresan et al. (2008), J. Electrochem. Soc. 155(6), A576

alpha_c.note: Capacity temperature coefficient; Li-S capacity strongly increases with T due to polysulfide dissolution
alpha_c.source: Wild et al. (2015), Energy Environ. Sci. 8, 3477

dOCV_dT.note: POSITIVE entropic coefficient for Li-S; unique among battery chemistries. The Li + 0.5S -> 0.5Li2S reaction has a positive entropy change (dS/dxi > 0) yielding dOCV/dT > 0, approx +0.35 mV/K. This means the cell is cooled during discharge (reversible endothermic).
dOCV_dT.source: Kumaresan et al. (2008), J. Electrochem. Soc. 155(6), A576; Cuisinier et al. (2014), J. Phys. Chem. Lett. 5, 3227

current.note: Negative=charge, Positive=discharge; Li-S limited to ~2C due to polysulfide shuttle

temperature.note: -15 to 60 degC; lower bound due to electrolyte freezing
